programme.title: Woman at the end of the world

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: There are still places where education remains a luxury that many children can only dream of.These include Bangladesh - a small country in South Asia, one of the most densely populated and poorest in the world.An area twice as large as Poland is inhabited by as many as 170 million people.At the same time, 20% of the population lives below the poverty line.Obtaining an education gives you a chance to improve your financial situation.Unfortunately, the monsoons that hit Bangladesh every year cut off 1/4 of its area from the rest of the world, including schools.To help thousands of children, squares, libraries and educational centers were created... on boats.He studies there, among others:Rabija, the youngest heroine of Martyna Wojciechowska's program so far.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska goes to Prague, Czech Republic, where she plans to talk about... sex.The heroine of the episode is Vladana Augsten, a professional who treats sexuality through touch.She is a certified sexual assistant for disabled people, one of eleven in the Czech Republic.In Switzerland, Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany, this profession is widely known, but in this post-communist country it appeared for the first time only five years ago.Organizations training people involved in it also received funding from the state.One of them is the Freya Foundation.The sexuality of disabled people remains a taboo.Parents not only avoid the topic, but even make it difficult for their children to establish closer relationships, wanting to spare them pain and disappointment.The goal of Vladana and other sexual assistants is to support clients in their pursuit of independence.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska goes to Pakistan, where she meets members of the Kalash tribe.They are the only non-Muslim community in this country, the last descendants of the inhabitants of ancient Kafiristan, who inhabit the lands located on the border of today's Pakistan and Afghanistan.Only about four thousand of them survived.Kalaska women choose their own husbands, and when they do not treat them well or the relationship does not work out, they leave to look for a new partner.Free relationships are also allowed among the Kalash, which are prohibited in any other Pakistani community.
